prompt: a colour field sketch of a single bird, as a birder would draw it from life and finish in the studio: a light pencil underdrawing carrying clean watercolour washes and coloured-pencil detail, worked up sharply where identification lives — head, bill, eye, wing pattern, the edges of each feather tract — and left looser and more sketchy toward the tail, belly and legs, a few pencil strokes still showing; true proportions and a faithful likeness of the species, natural unsaturated colours, soft daylight; the bird alone on plain white paper, no border, no caption, no text. A Common Scoter (Melanitta nigra), a member of the family Anatidae (Ducks, Geese, and Swans), perched on a small branch, wings folded neatly against the body, side profile. Identification — emphasise these field marks: Bulky all-black sea duck; male entirely glossy black with a knob at the bill base; bill black with a yellow-orange patch on the upper ridge. Dark legs, pointed tail. Render the legs and feet accurately: short legs set fairly far back, with fully webbed front toes; legs and feet often orange, grey or black. Keep the likeness of the bird in the reference photo: same proportions, bill and head shape, posture, plumage pattern and colour tones — a portrait of this species, not a generic or idealised bird. Draw the bird only: leave out everything around it in the photo — habitat, foliage, branches, grass, water, sky, rocks, snow, fences, wires, feeders, hands, rings, other birds — on plain white, no cast shadow, no backdrop; at most the barest neutral perch under its feet. A typical wild adult in natural, muted colours, the whole bird in frame, uncropped, both legs and feet visible. anatomically correct, exactly two wings in a natural realistic position with properly layered flight feathers, correct wing orientation, natural posture.
